rounds.proof_sketch: With elements_per_block=256 and blockDim.x=256, the mutated <= causes thread 0 to process one extra element at index (bid+1)*256. This element is either (a) out of bounds (caught by break) or (b) the same element processed by the next block's thread 0. Both threads compute identical values (same avg pool calculation on same input window), so writing twice yields identical results.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the loop upper bound from < to <=, causing thread 0 of each block to potentially execute one additional iteration. This extra iteration either processes an out-of-bounds index (caught by the bounds check `if (linear_idx >= total_output_elements) break;`) or processes an element that another thread also processes. Since average pooling is deterministic and both threads compute the same input window's average, they write identical values to the same output location. Multiple writes of identical values produce correct results in CUDA. The output tensor is initialized to zeros, so no stale data interferes.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation causes redundant computation that writes identical values, never producing different output. No value-level input can expose a difference because the duplicate writes always compute and store the same result.
rounds.recommendations: When testing loop bound mutations (< vs <=), verify whether the extra iteration performs redundant but correct work vs. accessing invalid memory or computing wrong results. Mutations that only add duplicate writes of identical values are equivalent mutants and should be filtered by static analysis detecting deterministic pure computations.
